newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end off on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end off on profit-taking.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended lower on Monday after light profit-taking weighed on a thin-volume market, dealers and analysts said.
"There has been profit-taking relative to positions acquired some time ago," said Lars Schonander, head of research at Santander Investment-Mexico.
"The market is still 1.3 percent higher compared to one week ago," he added.
The leading IPC share index ended down 10.24 points, or 0.22 percent, at 4,712.18.
Schonander said buyers were absent due to concerns over a strong peso rather than any widespread disappointment over second quarter earnings reports.

"We have seen weakness in companies that posted good numbers, so it is hard to say reports are moving the market... There is some concern over the strong peso, and that has thwarted investment flows," he said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts meanwhile closed 1.2 centavos weaker on the day but were still close to their strongest level for the year at 7.7990/7.8010 per dollar.
Trading volume was a mediocre 66.1 million shares, of which two cross trades accounted for 12 million.
Traders said international investors had shunned the Mexican bourse to buy into sharp gains posted by blue chips traded in Sao Paulo, where the Bovespa index ended up 3.3 percent to 12,938 points.
"Brazil was hot today, and that could haul us up tomorrow or the day after, but for now it kept players away from Mexico," a floor trader said.
Dealers said media group Televisa and building firm Empresas ICA weighed most on the market.
Televisa shed 3.00 pesos to 113.00 pesos as dealers took profits notched up after strong earnings posted last week, dealers said.

ICA fell 1.25 pesos to 21.45 pesos despite what dealers said were reasonable earnings posted during the session. They suggested investors preferred to take profits while waiting for the Mexican government to announce a restructuring plan for toll highway concessions.
On the broad market, declining issues outnumbered gainers by 55 to 41 out of 121 stocks that changed hands.
